title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
An AI music generation system was trained on copyrighted music without the permission of rights holders. The system generated original compositions from text prompts, but its training process involved the unauthorized use of existing recordings. This represents a model deployment failure where the training dataset was sourced without establishing proper licensing agreements beforehand.

The failure occurred during the development phase, before the system was offered to users. What would have caught this: securing licensing agreements with major record labels before training the model, or implementing a review process to verify that all training data had legitimate rights clearance. Instead, the system was deployed and then settlements were negotiated after legal action.

It is not established what financial penalties resulted or whether all copyright claims have been resolved. Lawsuits from other rights holders remained active at the time of reporting.

summary:
# Summary

Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio by reaching licensing agreements. The dispute centered on allegations that Udio used copyrighted songs without permission to train its artificial intelligence system, which generates original music from text prompts. Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year trained exclusively on authorized and licensed music, allowing users to customize, stream and share songs. Financial terms were not disclosed.

This marks Udio's first music licensing deal with a major label. Udio's CEO stated the collaboration would help unite AI and the music industry while supporting artists. Artists can choose to participate in the new platform and will receive compensation, though specific details were withheld. The settlement demonstrates how entertainment companies are working with AI startups to address copyright concerns while exploring new business opportunities in music creation.
